title: Tenali Raman and the Royal Falconer's Wager

full_text:
The King’s chief royal falconer, an arrogant man named Shaukat, boasted that his prize hunting falcon, Toofan, was the fiercest, fastest predator in the skies. He trained his birds through starvation and harsh whipping, mocking the palace pigeon-keepers who raised gentle homing doves.
Shaukat boasted:
'Gentle birds are cowards! Only beasts ruled by fear and hunger possess true skill!
My falcon can intercept and bring down any bird in Vijayanagara within two minutes of release!'

Tenali Raman smiled:
'Shaukat, love and gentle patience build stronger wings than cruelty and starvation.
I wager that a simple, gentle homing dove raised with affection can outfly your fiercest falcon!'

The wager was accepted before King Krishnadevaraya on the palace terraces.
Shaukat brought forward his fierce falcon, hooded, talons sharpened, screeching hungrily.
Tenali brought a modest, snow-white homing dove named Shanti, which perched calmly upon his wrist, cooing affectionately and pecking sweet millet from his palm.

The signal was given!
Tenali released the white dove into the sky.
Shaukat unhooded his fierce falcon, shouting: 'Strike, Toofan! Slay the dove!'
The falcon soared into the air with lightning speed, its talons extended, diving directly at the white dove!

Any ordinary bird would have panicked and fluttered into the open air to be shredded.
However, Tenali had trained the dove through patient love: whenever danger appeared, the dove knew that safety lay in diving straight into the deep, thorny bougainvillea trellis on the palace terrace!
The dove folded its wings, plummeted like a white stone, and darted safely into the dense, maze-like thorns of the thick bougainvillea bush!

The fierce falcon, blinded by aggressive hunger and flying too fast to pull up, crashed headlong into the dense, thorny brambles!
Its wings were tangled, its feathers plucked, and it struggled helplessly among the thorns, squawking in panic!

Tenali gently reached his hand into the safe inner hollow of the bush:
The little white dove hopped calmly onto his fingers, completely unhurt, cooing softly!

Tenali freed the tangled falcon, smoothed its bruised feathers, and handed it back to the humiliated falconer:
'Look, Shaukat! Thy falcon was driven by blind, starving fury, and crashed into ruin.
My dove was guided by calm trust and loving intelligence, finding safe refuge in an instant!
Cruelty blinds the eyes, but patience and gentle affection conquer the skies.'

The King praised Tenali’s gentle wisdom, awarded him the prize, and ordered the royal falconry to abandon harsh training methods in favor of humane care.
moral: Cruelty and arrogance toward gentle creatures are defeated by patient training and natural devotion.
